title: Naturality of Verschiebung and its value on diagonalizable groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p>0$. All groups are commutative affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Use the twist $G^{(p)}$ and canonical $V_G:G^{(p)}\to G$ of [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung]. For every group homomorphism $f:G\to H$, one has $fV_G=V_Hf^{(p)}$. Formation of $V$ commutes with arbitrary extensions of the ground field and with finite products, under the canonical product and twist identifications. Consequently, if $V_G=0$, then $V_N=0$ for every closed subgroup $N\subseteq G$, and $V_Q=0$ for every quotient homomorphism $G\to Q$ that is faithfully flat and finitely presented (that is, an epimorphism of represented fppf sheaves, for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras). If $M$ is a finitely generated abelian group and $D_k(M)=\operatorname{Spec}k[M]$, where $k[M]$ has basis $e_m$, product $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$ and coproduct $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, then $V_{D_k(M)}$ is an isomorphism: its coordinate map sends $e_m$ to $e_m\otimes1$ in $k[M]^{(p)}$. Tensor products and spectra are [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No smoothness, connectedness or perfection is assumed.

source.place: Definition 11.39, properties (a)-(c), printed pp.224-225; diagonalizable specialization of its invariant-tensor construction, with the group-algebra Hopf structure in Chapter 12. Subgroup and quotient consequences use the represented fppf quotient convention of Chapter 5.

proof.text:
Put $C=k[G]$, $A=k[H]$ and $h=f^*:A\to C$. The construction [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung] gives $v_C=\lambda_C\Delta_{p,C}$ and $v_A=\lambda_A\Delta_{p,A}$. Pulling back the homomorphism identity $f m_G=m_H(f\times f)$ gives $\Delta_C h=(h\otimes h)\Delta_A$, using the tensor pushout and affine spectrum correspondence. Iteration gives $\Delta_{p,C}h=h^{\otimes p}\Delta_{p,A}$. The naturality formula of [lem-sfb-symmetric-invariant-frobenius-projection] now gives
$$v_C h=\lambda_C I_p(h)\Delta_{p,A}=h^{(p)}\lambda_A\Delta_{p,A}=h^{(p)}v_A.$$
The faithful affine spectrum correspondence reverses this equality to $fV_G=V_Hf^{(p)}$.

source.place: Definition 11.39(a), printed p.224; explicit coordinate proof of functoriality

proof.text:
For a field extension $k\to K$, put $C_K=C\otimes_k K$. The tensor pushout and scalar-extension definitions give the twist comparison
$$\theta:(C_K)^{(p)}\xrightarrow{\sim}C^{(p)}\otimes_k K,\qquad (c\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto(c\otimes1)\otimes a^pb.$$
Its inverse sends $(c\otimes d)\otimes a$ to $(c\otimes1)\otimes da$ ($d\in k$, viewed in $K$). These formulas respect both balancing relations, and composing either way is the identity because $(a x)\otimes b=x\otimes a^pb$ in the twist. Thus no inverse to Frobenius on either field is used. A $k$-basis $B$ of $C$ extends to the $K$-basis $\{b\otimes1:b\in B\}$: finite tensor sums expand in these vectors, and the coefficient maps associated to $B$ prove their independence. The same argument on tensor powers shows that extension of scalars identifies the orbit-sum bases of $I_p(C)\otimes_k K$ and $I_p(C_K)$.

source.place: Definition 11.39(c), printed p.225; explicit twist and invariant-space comparisons

proof.text:
On a singleton orbit $b^{\otimes p}$, the two maps $\theta\lambda_{C_K}$ and $\lambda_C\otimes1$ of the preceding comparison both give $(b\otimes1)\otimes1$; on each non-singleton orbit sum both give zero. By the orbit-basis formula in [lem-sfb-symmetric-invariant-frobenius-projection] they agree on every invariant tensor. The comultiplication on $C_K$ is obtained by extending that on $C$: on $c\otimes a$, its iterated value is $\Delta_{p,C}(c)$ with scalar $a$ in one factor, by pulling back the base-changed multiplication. Consequently
$$\theta v_{C_K}(c\otimes a)=v_C(c)\otimes a.$$
The construction of $v$ and the affine spectrum correspondence identify this equality with the claimed base-change compatibility of $V$.

source.place: Definition 11.39(c), printed p.225; comparison of the orbit formula with iterated comultiplication

proof.text: For $G\times H$, its coordinate algebra is $C\otimes_k A$: maps to it as an affine scheme are pairs of algebra maps by the tensor pushout property. The same property identifies $(G\times H)^{(p)}$ with $G^{(p)}\times H^{(p)}$, the coordinate isomorphism sending $(c\otimes a)\otimes d$ to $(c\otimes1)\otimes(a\otimes d)$. Apply step 1 to the two projections $\pi_G,\pi_H$. The two components of $V_{G\times H}$ are then $V_G\pi_G^{(p)}$ and $V_H\pi_H^{(p)}$, so the product universal property identifies it with $V_G\times V_H$. Iterate for any nonempty finite product. For the empty product, the terminal group has only one endomorphism, which proves the assertion as well.

source.place: Definition 11.39(b), printed p.225; projections and the product universal property

proof.text: Suppose $V_G=0$ and let $i:N\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup. Step 1 gives $iV_N=V_Gi^{(p)}=0=i0$. For every $k$-algebra $R$, the map $i(R)$ is injective by the subgroup definition [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], hence $V_N(R)=0$. As $N^{(p)}$ is affine, evaluate this equality at its coordinate ring and at its universal point; the affine spectrum correspondence then gives $V_N=0$ as a morphism. This argument uses injectivity on all algebra-valued points, not only on points valued in fields.

source.place: Definition 11.39(a), printed p.224, applied to closed subgroups (Chapter 5 subgroup convention)

proof.text:
Let $q:G\to Q$ be a quotient of the stated kind and put $E=k[Q]$. The coordinate map $u:E\to C$ is faithfully flat. Its Frobenius twist $u^{(p)}:E^{(p)}\to C^{(p)}$ is its base change along $E\to E^{(p)}$, $e\mapsto e\otimes1$: the tensor pushout identifies
$$C\otimes_E E^{(p)}\simeq C\otimes_{k,\sigma}k,\qquad c\otimes(e\otimes a)\longmapsto c\,u(e)\otimes a,$$
with inverse $c\otimes a\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes a)$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] makes $u^{(p)}$ faithfully flat. Taking the module $E^{(p)}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] shows that $u^{(p)}$ is injective. Step 1 and $V_G=0$ give $V_Qq^{(p)}=0q^{(p)}$. On coordinate maps this is $u^{(p)}v_E=u^{(p)}0^*$, so injectivity yields $v_E=0^*$ and hence $V_Q=0$. Finite presentation is part of the quotient convention; the cancellation itself only needs faithful flatness.

source.place: Definition 11.39(a), printed p.224, quotient consequence; algebraic cancellation uses Stacks Tags 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change) and 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective)

proof.text:
For $C=k[M]$ with the displayed Hopf structure, iteration gives $\Delta_p(e_m)=e_m^{\otimes p}$. The singleton-orbit formula in [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung] therefore gives $v_C(e_m)=e_m\otimes1$. Define a $k$-linear map $w:C^{(p)}\to C$ by
$$w\bigl((\sum_m a_me_m)\otimes c\bigr)=\sum_m a_m^p c\,e_m.$$
The sums are finite. The formula is additive, and the balancing relation $(ra)\otimes c=a\otimes r^pc$ shows it is well-defined. Its product formula follows from $(\sum_{m+n=t}a_mb_n)^p=\sum_{m+n=t}a_m^pb_n^p$, so $w$ is a unital $k$-algebra map. Now $wv_C(e_m)=e_m$, and
$$v_Cw\bigl((\sum_m a_me_m)\otimes c\bigr)=\sum_m(e_m\otimes a_m^pc)=(\sum_m a_me_m)\otimes c.$$
Thus $w$ and $v_C$ are mutual inverses. Applying affine spectrum proves that $V_{D_k(M)}$ is an isomorphism with precisely the asserted coordinate formula. This includes $M=0$, infinite $M$ with finite support in each element, and $p$-torsion in $M$; in the item $M$ is finitely generated.
